ActionId.description: Identifies one dispatched Action inside a Run (RS-15).

AdmissionResult.description:
What `validate(spec, binding, registry)` returns. It touches no hardware.

Rule: SB-38.

coercions_preview.description: What the Providers said they would change (SB-7, SB-44).

matched.description: Spec resource name — and `needs` name — to the resolved `ResourceId` (SB-36).

rejected.description: Constraints the bound instance could not satisfy (SB-38).

ArtifactMark.description: One `mark_artifact` reaction recorded against an artifact (RS-30).

ArtifactRef.description:
Large data is always by reference: a locator, a content hash and a size, never
the bytes (RS-44, Vision §50, §51).

continuity.description:
The continuity metadata of SC-30, in SampleClock order. There is more than
one whenever the capture spans a rate change (TM-13c) or a channel-count
change (SC-30a): each ends one map and starts the next (RS-40).

id.description: The artifact's name inside its Run (SB-17).

kind.description: Its kind; a Sink Module's namespace (MA-25).

partial.description: True when it was still open at cleanup, or the Run aborted (RS-26, RS-44).

BackPressure.description: What a link does when its queue is at capacity. There is no default (SC-19).

oneOf.description:
Publishing is refused as full and nothing is ever dropped.
The name is the Vision's; the policy produces back-pressure through a
refusal the producer must honour, not through a parked thread (SC-20a).
The oldest queued block is evicted (SC-20).

BindingSection.description:
The `binding` section: the BindingProfile, `environment` included, as parsed and
re-serialised canonically from the parsed document (RS-38, RS-45, SB-27).

ChannelGap.description: A channel that lost validity while the stream continued (SC-31d).

ChildRecord.description: One child Run a Session created (RS-25a).

manifest.description: The child's Manifest hash; absent when it could not be sealed (RS-46).

seq.description: The `RunChild` entry of the parent's action log (RS-15).

CleanupFailure.description:
A cleanup step that failed or timed out. Every step is attempted even when an
earlier one failed; each failure is recorded and the sequence continues (RS-6).

fragment.description: Which fragment, for a per-fragment step (RS-8).

timed_out.description:
Whether it was abandoned on its deadline rather than returning an error
(RS-8a).

CleanupMode.description: Whether a stop delivers the declared tail (RS-9).

oneOf.description: The Provider delivers its declared tail (RS-9).

CleanupStep.description:
The seven ordered steps of RS-6, each named for what it does, not the unordered
list of Vision §53.

oneOf.description:
1. Freeze dispatch and cancel every pending burst and timer. This precedes
   stopping the Providers: a burst still queued when a transmitter stops will
   reopen it on a device that honours timed commands (RS-7).
2. Stop every Provider, in reverse dependency order (RS-8).

3. Drain the stepped instances under `orderly`, then stop every Executor and
   Sink, in reverse dependency order (RS-8, RS-9).
4. Restore baseline state, in reverse dependency order (RS-8).

5. Drain the event path, then finalise artifacts, marking as partial anything
   still open (RS-6, RS-30, RS-44).
6. Drain the event path again and collect the counters (RS-6, RS-35).
7. Release the Lease and write the Manifest (RS-6, RS-11).

ClockDomain.description:
A registered clock domain. Immutable once registered, except that `ended_at`
may be set once (TM-12).

ended_at.description: When the domain stopped advancing, in root ticks; set once, by a rate change (TM-13c).

kind.description: Root or Derived, with its rate or ratio (TM-3).

local.description: Node-local ordinal, allocated by the owning registry.

node.description: Owning node; `0`, the local node, throughout v4.0 (X7).

ClockDomainKind.description:
A domain is either a timekeeper of its own or an exact division of one (TM-3).

A `Derived` domain names a `Root` directly; there are no chains (decision T2).

oneOf.description: A timekeeper: a tick rate and what tick zero means.

epoch.description: What tick zero is anchored to.

tick_rate.description: Ticks per second; neither term may exceed 2^31 (TM-3).

oneOf.description: An exact division of a root, such as a SampleClock (TM-10, TM-13a).

origin.description: This domain's tick zero, expressed in root ticks (decision T2).

root.description: The `Root` this divides; refused if unknown or itself `Derived` (TM-3).

root_ticks_per_tick.description: Root ticks per one tick here; neither term may exceed 2^31 (TM-3).

ClockRelation.description:
A measured relation between two roots: the only path between domains that are
not exactly related, and the record every Run carries from its root to `utc`.

`drift` and `drift_uncertainty` are the only floating-point quantities in the
time model, and neither reaches a stored `TimePoint` unrounded (TM-14, X9).

Rule: TM-5, TM-14, TM-18. Vision §24, §50.

drift.description:
Dimensionless: target seconds per source second, minus 1. Refused when
non-finite, because `serde_json` would otherwise write it as `null` and a
NaN drift would share a Manifest hash with one that was never measured
(OV-15, X9).

drift_uncertainty.description:
Dimensionless, non-negative: the one-sided error bound on `drift`. Zero
claims the drift is known exactly and is expected to be rare. Refused when
non-finite (OV-15, X9).

measured_at.description: When the measurement was taken, in the source domain.

method.description: Namespaced name of the measurement method, for example `dev.pps_poll`.

offset.description: The image of `measured_at` in the target domain.

uncertainty.description: The bound at `measured_at`, in target ticks, before drift error accumulates.

valid.description: The window over which the relation may be applied.

relations.description: Every relation, including the Run's root to UTC with its uncertainty (TM-18).

sample_clocks.description: One record per SampleClock, in order, per stream (TM-13d).

Coercion.description: A value the Provider changed, with its reason (SB-44).

reason.description: The Provider's reason, uninterpreted by the Kernel.

Constraint.description:
What a Spec requires of a key. Its value is a [`Scalar`]: a constraint over a
list or a map cannot be written, because the matcher would then need the
Vocabulary's semantics to compare them.

Rule: SB-5, decision B1.

oneOf.description: Within these bounds, either of which may be absent.
The key is declared at all.

ContentHash.description:
`sha256:<64 lowercase hex>`, matching `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$`. The algorithm is
named in the value so a later algorithm is an additive change (OV-14, SB-1).

ContinuityMap.description:
What a stream carried, per SampleClock. There is one map per SampleClock: a
block in another domain ends the map, and the Sink starts a new builder (SC-30).

channels.description: The channel count, constant for the map (SC-30a).

end.description: Just past the last sample the map accounts for (SC-30).

first.description: First sample the map accounts for: a first block's leading gap included (SC-30).

valid.description: Per channel, the runs of valid samples (SC-14, SC-30).

CounterRow.description: One row of the never-dropping counter table (RS-33).

count.description: How many were emitted, whether or not the body survived (RS-33).

source.description: Which resource, or the fallback row's placeholder (RS-33).

DataContractId.description:
A namespaced contract id matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)+$`,
for example `ezsdr.stream.cf32`.

Rule: SB-1, SC-2.

DataLinkDecl.description:
A declared link: its endpoints, the contract it carries, its policy and its
capacity in blocks (SC-19).

capacity.description: Queue depth in blocks, at least 1 (SC-19).

contract.description: The contract carried; SC-3 checks it against both ports (SC-19).

policy.description: What happens at capacity; there is no default (SC-19).

DataLinkId.description:
Identifies a data link instance (`DataLinkDecl`).

Rule: SC-18 (`02-stream-contract.md`), X7.

local.description: Node-local ordinal, allocated by the owning registry.

node.description: Owning node; `0`, the local node, throughout v4.0 (X7).

Duration.description:
An elapsed time: integer ticks in a named clock domain (TM-1, TM-4 decision T4).

The domain tag is what stops 1 000 ticks at 20 Msps being added to a 200 MHz
point as a silent factor-of-ten error.

EnvelopeFidelity.description:
The value set MA-42 gives timing and continuity: `none < envelope <
hardware_quirk < real`. `real` is added to Vision §14's sets, which stop at
`hardware_quirk` and leave a Hardware Run with nothing to record although the
same section says every Run records the vector.

Rule: MA-42.

oneOf.description: Not modelled at all; an `ideal` Mock profile declares this (Vision §13).
A specific hardware quirk is emulated.

EpochRef.description: What a domain's tick zero is anchored to (TM-3).

oneOf.description:
Tick zero is whatever set it; the string names the mechanism, for example
`uhd.set_time_now` or `sim.run_start` (Vision §15, §50; OV-23a: a
named example, not a Kernel dependency).

set_by.description: Namespaced name of whatever established the epoch.

oneOf.description:
Tick zero is the PPS edge at which `set_by` set the time, and the root is locked to
the PPS's reference, so every whole second of the root is a PPS edge (TM-3).

set_by.description: Namespaced name of whatever set the time at that edge.

Event.description:
The control-path form of an event: a source, a `TimePoint` in a named domain, a
severity, a kind and a schema-versioned payload (Vision §29).

Rule: RS-31.

payload.description: The body; its schema belongs to the kind's owner (RS-31).

EventKind.description:
What kind of event this is, matching `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*(\.[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*)+$`:
every kind is namespaced. The Kernel owns the five of RS-28, under `ezsdr.`, and
every other kind belongs to the Vocabulary or Module that emits it.

Rule: SB-1, RS-27.

EventsSection.description:
The `events` section: the complete counter table, including rows whose count is
zero, and the bodies that were delivered (RS-33, RS-38).

counters.description: Every `(source, kind)` row reachable in the plan (RS-33).

delivered.description: The bodies that survived the ring (RS-34).

ExecutionClass.description:
What kind of Run this is, derived from the environment and cross-checked against
the Authority's `Pacing`; a class that was merely declared could lie.

Rule: MA-41, RS-42. Vision §14.

oneOf.description: Simulation Engine, free-running, simulated RF path.
Simulation Engine, wall-paced, simulated RF path.
Device timekeeper, cabled or partly simulated RF path.

class.description:
Derived from the environment and cross-checked against the Authority's
pacing (MA-41, SB-39).

fragments.description: The fragments, already in dependency order (SB-39).

links.description:
The DataLink declarations: the graph's links, then the output feeds, numbered
on from them (SC-19, MA-27a, D75).

Fidelity.description:
What a Run's models actually claim, per aspect. A Run's value per aspect is the
**weakest** over its bound Providers, so a Hardware Run with a best-effort
MockPeripheral records `timing: envelope`.

Rule: MA-42, RS-41. Vision §14.

continuity.description: How faithfully continuity and gaps are modelled.

rf.description: How faithfully the RF path is modelled.

Finite.description:
A finite 64-bit float: NaN and the infinities are refused, so OV-15's
canonicaliser never meets one.

Rule: SB-4, OV-15.

Fragment.description: One unit of work handed to one Module at `prepare`, in dependency order (SB-39).

after.description: Fragments that must be prepared and armed first (SB-39).

content.description: What to do; namespaced content the Kernel does not interpret (SB-39).

instance.description: Which exact Module version performs it, as its binding names it (SB-22, D78).

Gap.description: An interval of missing samples in the stream (SC-30, Vision §28).

link_dropped.description:
How many blocks the link discarded inside the same interval. A block count,
not a sample count: the samples the link lost are `len − lost`, and are
unrecoverable when `lost` is absent. That is a real limit of what a dropped
header can tell us, not an omission (SC-20b, SC-31).

lost.description: What the stream reported losing, when known (SC-13).

GapCause.description:
What the **stream** lost. A closed, derived set (SC-31, decision S16).

What the **link** lost is the separate `link_dropped` count, not a cause, so a
device overflow inside an interval that also lost a block to the link is still
reported as `OverflowRestart` with its sample count, beside a link-drop count of
one. Collapsing the two into a single cause loses the device's own diagnosis.

oneOf.description: `RESTARTED`: a stream restart, as a UHD overflow produces (SC-31, OV-23a).
`ALIGNMENT`: samples the device discarded to keep its channels aligned (SC-31).
A jump with no gap flag on a lossy path (SC-31).

`GAP_BEFORE` with `lost` less than the jump on a lossy path and no carry to
explain the difference (SC-31).

stream_lost.description: What the stream itself reported losing.

Ident.description:
A name inside one document, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`.

Names are compared as bytes; there is no case folding and no Unicode
normalisation, so the canonical form of OV-15 stays byte-comparable.

Rule: SB-1.

Key.description:
A `<vocabulary prefix><path>` or `ext.<module-id>.<path>` key: a Vocabulary key
matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)+$` and an Extension key
`^ext(\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+){2,}$`; a key beginning `ext.` is read as an Extension key only.

The Kernel checks the prefix and the value's shape against the `KeyDecl` and
never interprets the meaning (audit Finding 7).

Rule: SB-1, SB-2, MA-34.

LeaseMode.description: Whether a Run survives its client's disconnection (RS-21).

oneOf.description: The Run ends when the client disconnects. The default (RS-21, RS-23).
The Run survives the disconnect until the TTL expires (RS-21, RS-23).

ttl_ms.description: How long, on the host monotonic clock (RS-22).

LeaseRecord.description:
What the Manifest records of a Lease: its mode and whether it was released. The
token and the expiry deadline are runtime state only: the token is the credential
adoption checks (R5), and the deadline is a host monotonic instant with no
meaning outside the process (RS-22).

Rule: RS-38.

LinkRecord.description:
One DataLink the Run created, with what it dropped; its endpoints are its entry
in `plan.links` (RS-38, SC-20a).

drops.description: How many blocks it dropped; absent when cleanup never read it (RS-6).

LogEntry.description: One entry of the action log (RS-15).

seq.description:
Dense: a rejected Action occupies one too, because a log with holes cannot
be replayed or audited (RS-15).

time.description: The Run-time instant at which it arrived (RS-15).

ModuleId.description:
Names a Module implementation in the registry, matching
`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+(\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)*$`, at most 256 bytes.

The reverse-DNS-ish namespaced form (`ezsdr.test.provider`) is what keeps two
vendors' Modules from colliding; the Kernel checks the shape, not the authority.

Rule: SB-1, MA-31.

ModuleRef.description: A Module by id and version (MA-31).

Namespace.description:
A dotted sequence of `Ident`s owned by a Vocabulary or a Module,
matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)*$`.

Rule: SB-1.

NodeId.description:
A node in the (future) multi-host deployment. `0` (the local node) is the only legal value in v4.0.

Rule: X7 (`00-overview.md`); it qualifies every id of TM-11, SC-6, SB-3 and MA-38.

Outcome.description: What `admit()` decided about one Session Action (RS-15, RS-16).

oneOf.description: It passed every check and was dispatched (RS-16).

coercions.description: What was coerced, including RS-19's "as soon as possible" (SB-44).

dispatched.description: The Kernel Actions it compiled to (RS-14).

oneOf.description: It was refused and never reached the real-time path (RS-16).

Policy.description: A compiled reaction table for one Run (RS-26).

severities.description: Kind to severity, which RS-29 falls back to (RS-28).

PortRef.description: Names one port of one component instance (SC-1).

component.description: The component, Spec resource or output the port belongs to (SB-15, SB-22a).

port.description: The port name on that component (SC-1).

coercions.description:
What the Provider changed; these must equal what `coerce` returned for the
same request (MA-12, SB-44).

effective.description:
The applied configuration. `effective` may narrow a declared capability and
must not widen one (MA-12).

reports.description: One report per fragment, in plan order (SB-41).

PreviewedCoercion.description:
A coercion the Kernel previewed by calling one Provider's `coerce`, together with
the Spec resource whose request produced it.

A `Coercion` names a key and two values and nothing else, because a Provider
answers about the request it was handed. The Kernel's own record has to say more:
two resources may constrain one key on two different devices, and one of them
coercing says nothing about the other. Keyed on the key alone, `prepare`'s SB-44
check charged one resource's coercion to every resource naming that key and
refused a value `coerce` was never asked about — so the resource name is part of
the record, as it already is in `RejectedConstraint`.

Rule: SB-7, SB-38, SB-44.

coercion.description: What that resource's Provider said it would change (SB-7).

resource.description: The Spec resource whose `requires` map was coerced (SB-44).

ProfileRef.description:
A declared profile, by name and version. Vision §59 bumps a Mock profile's
version on measurement.

Rule: SB-22, MA-33 (decision B7).

Rational.description:
A positive rational, stored reduced by the greatest common divisor.

`num > 0`, `den > 0`, `gcd(num, den) = 1`, so equality is structural. Every
operation evaluates with 128-bit intermediates and returns an error rather than
wrapping, saturating or panicking.

Rule: TM-2.

Reaction.description:
One of exactly four reactions. It is a table: there is no expression language
and no rules engine, and logic that needs conditions belongs in a Reactor or in
client orchestration.

Rule: RS-26.

oneOf.description: Record the kind and time against every artifact open at that moment (RS-30).

RejectedConstraint.description: A constraint the bound instance could not satisfy (SB-38).

resource.description: The Spec resource whose constraint failed.

ResourceId.description:
Names a resource, or a sub-resource, inside the composite tree a Provider declares.

The path is a non-empty sequence of segments matching
`^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+){0,15}$`, at most 256 bytes; `dev0/rx/0` names
channel 0 of the receive sub-tree of `dev0`. Vision §49 asks only for the node qualification; the
path replaces §49's flat `local` because a channel or a timekeeper must be
addressable (`00-overview.md` "Where these specs depart from the Vision").

Rule: SB-1, SB-3, SB-33, SB-34 (`03-spec-and-binding.md`), X7.

node.description: Owning node; `0`, the local node, throughout v4.0 (X7).

path.description: Slash-joined path through the composite resource tree (SB-34).

Role.description:
The five roles. There is exactly one trait each and no shared lifecycle
supertrait: one trait forced onto radios and executors alike is what audit
Finding 22 rejects, and Link and Authority have no lifecycle at all.

Rule: MA-1, MA-2.

RunId.description:
Identifies one Run, unique per host (`04-run-and-session.md` RS-1, X6).

The form is `<node>:<pid-hex>:<unix-nanos-hex>-<counter>`. The process id is
required: `node` is fixed at `LOCAL` for all of v4.0 and the counter is
per-process, so without it two `ezsdr` processes on one host produce identical
ids within one nanosecond. Ceiling: unique per host, not across hosts until
`NodeId` is real (`00-overview.md` §8).

RunKind.description: What kind of Run this is (RS-1, RS-12).

oneOf.description: A Session, whose Spec is implicit and hashed like any other (RS-12).

children.description: The child Runs this Session created, in creation order (RS-25a).

deterministic.description: May be claimed only for the Simulation class with a recorded seed (RS-42).

execution_class.description:
Fixed at binding resolution and never changed during the Run; absent when no
plan was built, since the plan derives it (RS-42).

fidelity.description: The weakest value per aspect over the bound Providers (RS-41, MA-42).

parent.description: The parent Run, for a child (RS-25).

transitions.description: Every state transition, with its runtime instant and host UTC time (RS-5).

RunState.description: The eight states of a Run (RS-2).

oneOf.description: Cleanup finished; a Manifest was written (RS-11).

SampleClockRecord.description: One SampleClock as the Manifest records it, one per clock, in order, per stream (TM-13d).

ended_at.description: The root tick at which the clock stopped, on a rate change (TM-13c).

nominal_rate.description: Samples per second, derived by TM-10.

origin.description: The root tick of sample zero (TM-13b, TM-13e).

stream.description: The stream that owns the clock (TM-13a).

anyOf.description: A signed 64-bit integer, written as an exact decimal by the canonicaliser (OV-15).

Scalar.description:
The one scalar type: a `Value`'s scalar, a constraint's and a capability's value,
and a `DataContract` attribute (SB-4, SB-5, SC-2).

Carries no tag (OV-13's carve-out): a scalar is the value an author wrote, not a
two-field object wrapping it.

Rule: SB-4, SB-6, SC-2.

Segment.description: A contiguous run of valid samples on one channel (SC-30).

SessionAction.description:
The Session action envelope: a closed set, and **not** the Kernel Action set.

The Kernel's Actions are what a Reactor emits into the real-time path, while a
lease operation or a recorder request is a control-path act with no real-time
meaning. Each Session Action compiles to zero or more Kernel Actions, or to a
Lease or Run operation.

Only the lifecycle verbs are the Kernel's; a domain verb is
a `vocabulary` Session action, and the Vocabulary that registers the verb
declares how it compiles. The Vision's §3 log sketch named `StartRepeat` and
`Capture` directly before Step 5; here they are `radio.start_repeat` and `sink.capture`,
because a Kernel that enumerated them would need a new variant for the first
peripheral sweep or calibration verb.

Rule: RS-13, RS-13a, decision R3.

oneOf.description: Generic over a namespaced key and value (RS-13a).
A domain verb, whose compilation its Vocabulary declares (RS-13a, RS-14).

at.description:
When. A Kernel field, not a param: SB-4 caps a `Value` at one level of
nesting and a `TimePoint` is two, so a time could not travel inside
`params` at all (RS-19).

ns.description: The Vocabulary that owns the verb.

oneOf.description: With a target it stops that resource; without one it stops the Run (RS-50).

target.description: The resource, or the Run when absent.

oneOf.description:
Reclaim a Detached Lease. Adoption by run id alone would let any client
seize a live transmitter (RS-24).

binding_hash.description:
The child's own profile, by hash: a Session's cannot serve a Spec Run
(RS-25a, D103).

Severity.description: How bad an event is; RS-29 derives a default reaction from it (Vision §29).

oneOf.description: Something is off but the Run continues.

SpecSection.description:
The `spec` section: the Spec as parsed and re-serialised with every default
written out, its hash, and the source hash its caller supplied (RS-38, RS-45).

source.description:
The hash of the code that generated the Spec, as `Assembly.spec_source`
supplied it: opaque, never read by the Kernel, and outside `hash` (SB-14,
RS-38).

Stage.description: Which pipeline stage a Run was in when it failed (RS-3).

StopCause.description: Why a Run stopped (RS-3, RS-23, RS-26).

oneOf.description: The Policy table reacted to an event (RS-26).

Termination.description:
How a Run ended. There is no `Failed` **state**: a failure is a termination
reached through `Stopping`, because a Run that failed and was not cleaned up is
a transmitter nobody turned off.

Rule: RS-2, RS-3, decision R1.

reason.description: Why: a string beginning with the rule that refused (KC-7).

also.description:
Every later end request that escalated the mode, failed or was a Policy
reaction, in request order, beside the first (RS-10, KC-32).

cleanup_failures.description:
Steps that failed or timed out; every step is attempted even when an earlier
one failed (RS-6, RS-8a).

TimePoint.description:
An instant: integer ticks in a named clock domain. Never floating-point seconds.

There is deliberately no `PartialOrd`: two points of different domains cannot be
compared at all, and `a < b` silently answering `false` is the bug class this
model exists to prevent (decision T3).

Rule: TM-1, TM-6.

ticks.description: Tick count relative to the domain's origin; a sample index in a SampleClock (TM-10).

TransitionRecord.description: One recorded transition, with its runtime instant and the host UTC time (RS-5).

at.description: When, in Run time; absent before an Authority exists (RS-5).

Validity.description: The window over which a `ClockRelation` may be applied (TM-14).

from.description: First instant, in the source domain, at which the relation holds.

to.description: Last instant, in the source domain; absent means the bound grows without limit.

anyOf.description: A map of scalars; its keys are ASCII (SB-9a).

Value.description:
A scalar, or a list or map of scalars. One level is the type: nothing deeper can
be built or parsed.

A Spec is data, not a document tree: one level is what a structured parameter
such as a capture request needs, and more invites the schema-inside-a-schema
that Vision §9 rejects.

Rule: SB-4.

key.description: Which key, when the violation names one.

Warning.description: A non-fatal note from a stage (SB-38, SB-41).

message.description: What it says; uninterpreted by the Kernel.

description:
A Kernel envelope with namespaced Module sections. The Kernel writes the
envelope; each Module writes its own section; no Provider-specific field ever
requires a Kernel change.

The Vision's §50 listed "random seeds" and an optional environment capture among
the envelope's contents before Step 5; neither is an envelope field here. The Kernel owns no
random number generator, so a seed is something the environment declared, and
the environment is already recorded under `binding.body`; the
environment capture has no Kernel-defined content at all, so it belongs under
`sections` as `ezsdr.capture` (RS-43).

Rule: RS-38…RS-47. Vision §50, Finding 19.

action_log.description: The Session action log; absent for a Spec Run (RS-15).

clocks.description: Domains, relations and SampleClock records (TM-13d, TM-18).

hash.description:
The Manifest's own hash, computed over the Manifest with this field removed
and stored beside it, never inside the hashed body. Skipped when absent, so
that the hashed text does not carry `"hash": null` — a consumer implementing
RS-46 as written would otherwise compute a different digest (RS-46, OV-17).

inputs.description:
Artifacts the Run consumed, by reference; a client waveform is ingested here
before the Action referencing it is admitted (RS-44a).

links.description: Every DataLink the Run created, in `plan.links` order (RS-38).

modules.description: The Modules and Vocabulary versions in use (RS-38).

policy.description:
The resolved event reactions and severities for this Run; absent when the Run
failed before its Policy compiled, as `plan` is absent when it failed before
